children: The leader of Weil, Gotshal & Manges's bankruptcy practice, which was once the law firm's crown jewel, will join rival Skadden Arps.

Skadden is set to announce Wednesday that it hired about 40 bankruptcy lawyers, including 11 partners, from Weil — a firm that helped shepherd some of the country's most high-profile bankruptcies and is now itself dissolving.

Matt Barr, who led Weil's bankruptcy practice and was also an influential voice on its management committee, will now head Skadden's restructuring group. The Wall Street Journal previously reported that Barr was in talks with Skadden. He will stay at Weil through the end of the year.
Several other firms were actively recruiting Barr and his team, including Cleary Gottlieb and Paul Weiss, the Journal previously reported.

Weil invented much of modern bankruptcy practice and spent years as a go-to adviser for corporations under duress. It has handled many of the country's largest and most complex restructuring matters, including Lehman Brothers, General Motors, and Washington Mutual.

Weil's leading position in the bankruptcy world was overtaken by larger competitors, and some of its best talent had been picked off. The firm overall had experienced stagnant growth in recent years, which was part of the reason that it started to crater as more partners eyed the exits. Many in the industry saw a bitter irony in the firm that had helped guide some of the country's largest corporations through bankruptcy now having to engineer its own demise.
Skadden historically had a strong bankruptcy practice, including handling matters for American Airlines, MGM, and Charter Communications, but it has lost ground to rivals in recent years.

Weil's decision to wind down last month left hundreds of lawyers looking for new roles. Since the wind down was announced, other firms including Simpson Thacher, Kirkland & Ellis Gibson Dunn, Paul Weiss and Cleary Gottlieb have also scooped up the firm's talent.

Barr was elevated to head of Weil's restructuring group in July. He is known for his work representing First Brands Group in its complex bankruptcy, as well as on major energy-related chapter 11 proceedings such as EP Energy, Talen Energy and Fieldwood Energy. He also handled the bankruptcy of CEC Entertainment, the parent company of Chuck E. Cheese.
